title: Media and Arts
description: Two lessons that argue: why a town needs its library (lesson 23) and why a music market can collapse in ten years (lesson 24). The language of the theme is parallel change - the pattern the + comparative ... , the + comparative ... , which ties two movements together (the longer a room stays open, the more readers come), including the halves that fall (the higher the price, the fewer singles), the shortened form with the verb and the subject dropped (the more, the merrier), and the two traps of building it with a superlative or with more in front of a short adjective; and polarity - some, any, no and none, that is, which of them a sentence may take once you know whether it is affirmative, negative or interrogative: some in an affirmative statement and in a question that is really an offer, an invitation or a request, any after a negative verb, after the near-negatives hardly, barely and scarcely, after if, after an expression of doubt, in a genuine question, and in an affirmative sentence where it means practically every; no as an adjective only and none as a pronoun only; the compounds someone, somebody, something, somewhere against anyone, anybody, anything, anywhere against no one, nobody, nothing, nowhere, each series following the rule of its own word; and the one law that governs all of them - English marks a negative once and only once, so I didn't see nobody has to become either I didn't see anybody or I saw nobody. Around them, the vocabulary of the two lessons (to wonder, civilisation, era, depth, to explore, to enlighten, expansion, lifeblood, crafts, to pay tribute to, literacy, shortage; performance, passion, plunge, decline, drop, release, casualty, doubt, to surpass, to blame, track, supremacy, to shun), how to read a short cultural press article and tell a claim from the detail that supports it, how to express an opinion and how to express a feeling or a liking, and step 2 of the career research project - preparing an interview with somebody who already does the job you want
